clues.title: Road: concrete is extremely common
text: **Concrete roads** are extremely common in the Philippines.
NOTE: Thailand also has a lot of concrete roads.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Concrete roads are everywhere. Thailand also has a lot of them.

clues.title: Driving side: right
text: The Philippines drives on the **right**.
NOTE: Within Southeast Asia, Cambodia, Laos, Taiwan and Vietnam also drive on the right.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Traffic drives on the right. Within Southeast Asia, Cambodia, Laos, Taiwan and Vietnam also drive on the right.

clues.title: Plate: white with black text, green tint on old ones
text: Standard white licence plates with black text are used for passenger vehicles. You can also find many older plates from the 2002 series, which are recognisable due to their **green tint**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Passenger cars have white plates with black text. Many older plates (the 2002 series) have a green tint.

clues.title: Pole: octagonal metal poles
text: **Octagonal metal poles** are quite common in the Philippines.
NOTE: They can sometimes be found in [Bangladesh](https://maps.app.goo.gl/LAQNfYnDxvMB8vTbA) and [some parts of Malaysia](https://maps.app.goo.gl/jCzCnTXETaJUq5Af9) as well.

images.caption: Rice field with poles; the red circle zooms in on an octagonal metal pole, left

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Octagonal metal poles are quite common. They sometimes appear in Bangladesh and parts of Malaysia.

clues.title: Pole: single insulator on a side bar
text: You will often see a single insulator at the top of a vertical bar which is attached to the side of a utility pole.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A single insulator on the top of a vertical bar attached to the side of the pole.

clues.title: Road lines: mixed yellow and white centre, orange tint
text: Middle road lines in the Philippines can be either yellow or white. In particular, you will often see combined **yellow and white** middle lines, which is not common in any other East Asian country.
Yellow road lines commonly have a distinct [**orange tint**](https://goo.gl/maps/vT9Mpun12cRGEgun7).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Centre lines can be yellow or white, and often yellow and white together, which no other East Asian country does. Yellow lines often look orange.

clues.title: Road: tall square yellow stones
text: These tall, square **yellow road stones** are unique to the Philippines.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Tall square yellow road stones, found only here.

clues.title: Chevron: red on white
text: Chevrons are typically **red on white**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Curve chevrons are red on white.

clues.title: Sign: red, orange or yellow signposts
text: Sign posts are often painted **red**, **orange** or **yellow**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Signposts are often painted red, orange or yellow.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycles everywhere
text: **Tuk-tuks**, also referred to as tricycles, are extremely common in the Philippines, in many areas they are more common than typical cars.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Three-wheeled tuk-tuks (tricycles) are extremely common, often more than cars.

clues.title: Language: lots of English signs
text: Although Filipino is the official language of the Philippines, **English** is extremely common to find on signs. It is the only major Southeast Asian country where you’re likely to come across English.

images.caption: Building with English signage advertising a medical clinic

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: English is extremely common on signs next to the local language. It is the only major Southeast Asian country where you are likely to see so much English.

clues.title: Google car: white with visible black roof (older camera)
text: In Generation 3 you can come across a white Street View car with the **black roof** clearly visible.
You may also come across a silvery grey car, which is also found in [Bhutan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/WWXr2nyNkq8i9Gna8).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In older Gen 3 coverage (blurrier, softer colours): a white car with a clearly visible black roof. A silvery grey car also appears, which Bhutan has too.

differs.how: Bhutan also has a silvery grey car

clues.title: Road: grain spread out to dry
text: It is somewhat common to see grains being spread out on roads to dry.
NOTE: This practice is also common in Vietnam.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Grain is somewhat commonly spread out on roads to dry. Vietnam does this too.

clues.title: Pole: black or white box with three letters
text: These black or white boxes are commonly seen on utility poles. Most of the time they feature a three letter abbreviation of the municipality you are in. The abbreviations will either have all three letters stand for the municipality, or the first two letters will abbreviate the municipality while the third letter indicates the province.
In the first image the "GMI" and "GMU" stands for the town of Gamu in the province of Isabela while the second image the "BGE" stands for the town of Bangued.
NOTE: Most towns do not have any standardised abbreviation so you might find many different abbreviations for the same place.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Black or white boxes on poles show a three-letter code for the town: either all three letters, or two for the town and one for the province. Many towns have no standard code.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycle designs vary by region
text: The Philippines have several different tuk-tuk and tricycle designs, roughly distributed as shown in this infographic.
_This image was provided by AeroGelo. You can click on the image to enlarge it._

images.caption: Tricycle roof designs by province: low, mid, high, umbrella and flat roofs, with a map

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Several different tricycle designs are spread across the country, as shown in the map.

clues.title: Sign: province names
text: **Province names** are very common to find on signs and can thus be very useful. However, they do not appear on the map, meaning they’re necessary to memorise in order to use them.
It is worth mentioning that Davao de Oro changed its name from Compostela Valley in 2019.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Province names are common on signs and very useful, but they are not on the map, so you must learn them. One province was renamed in 2019.

clues.title: Phone numbers: landline 0 + area code, mobile 09
text: Landlines will start with a 0 followed by the **area code**. Mobile phone numbers start with 09.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Landlines start with 0 then an area code. Mobile numbers start with 09.

clues.title: Plate: motorcycle colour strip shows region
text: Motorcycles in the Philippines have regional colour-coded plates as seen on this map. Notably, the northern half of the country has the coloured strip at the top, while the southern half has it on the bottom of the plate.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Motorcycle plates have a coloured strip that depends on the region. In the northern half the strip is at the top, in the southern half at the bottom.

clues.title: Landscape: dry pine mountains in the north
text: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat **dry mountainsides** and an abundance of **pine trees**. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in [Mindanao](https://maps.app.goo.gl/dowDy4SWZt1pvxtG9).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north: forested mountains with somewhat dry slopes and many pine trees. You may rarely see this on high roads in the far south island.

clues.title: Plants: corn, mostly in the north and far south
text: While **corn** can be found in most of the country, it is most common on northern Luzon and on Mindanao.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Corn grows in most of the country but is most common in the far north island and the big southern island.

clues.title: Plants: oil palm plantations in the south
text: The vast majority of **Oil palm** plantations are found on Mindanao.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most oil palm plantations are on the big southern island.

clues.title: Plants: sugarcane on two central islands
text: The majority of **sugarcane** in the Philippines can be found on the islands of Negros and Panay.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most sugarcane is on two islands in the centre-west.

clues.title: Plants: pineapple plantations in the south
text: **Pineapple **plantations are mostly found on Mindanao.

images.caption: Circle zooms in on pineapple plants in the field

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Pineapple plantations are mostly on the big southern island.

clues.title: Plants: banana plantations in the south
text: **Banana** plantations are almost exclusively found in central and southern Mindanao.
NOTE: Wild growing banana plants can be found all over the country, so make sure what you are seeing is an actual plantation before guessing.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Banana plantations are almost only in the centre and south of the big southern island. Wild bananas grow everywhere, so check it is a real plantation.

clues.title: Plants: pale-trunk trees with feathery tops
text: [Moluccan albizia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falcataria_falcata) are trees with **light coloured trunks **and [**pinnate leaves**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinnation) near the top of the tree. They are mainly found on Mindanao and are especially common in the eastern and central regions of the island.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Trees with light-coloured trunks and feathery leaves near the top. Mostly on the big southern island, especially the east and centre.

clues.title: Houses: woven bamboo walls with diamond pattern
text: Houses built with [amakan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amakan) walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a **diamond pattern** are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

images.caption: Bamboo house with woven diamond-pattern walls; the circle at top left magnifies the weave

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Houses with woven bamboo-mat walls in a diamond pattern are almost only in the southern half.

clues.title: Houses: woven bamboo walls, diagonal pattern
text: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a **diagonally woven pattern** are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

images.caption: Thatched-roof house on stilts with woven bamboo walls; the circle at top left magnifies the diagonal weave

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Woven bamboo walls with a diagonal weave are mostly on one western island but also across the northern half.

clues.title: Guardrail: yellow and black striped concrete
text: In the Cordillera Administrative Region you can find **yellow and black** striped concrete guardrails.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the northern mountain region: concrete guardrails with yellow and black stripes.

clues.title: Guardrail: white with three black stripes
text: White guardrails with **three recurring black stripes** are unique to the region of Bicol in southern Luzon.

images.caption: White guardrail with three black stripes; circle zooms in on the stripes

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: White guardrails with three repeating black stripes, unique to the south-east of the main northern island. Similar rails with more or fewer stripes exist, but three points to this area.

clues.title: Pole: square concrete with indented sides
text: Square concrete poles with an** indent **on both side, similar to the poles found in Chile, are mainly found north of Manila and in and around the city of Bacolod on the island of Negros.

images.caption: Concrete pole with indented sides; a red circle zooms in on the pole at left

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Square concrete poles with an indent on both sides, like Chile's. Mainly north of the capital and around one central island city.

clues.title: Pole: ladder-like top of two bars with thin wires
text: A poletop made up of two tall vertical metal bars having an [L-shaped cross-section](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tQrN9cdrQZshGuAQ6) which are connected via several thin wires, making it resemble a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area.

NOTE: You may sometimes come across [similar looking poletops](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HSfKKMtbuvh2JS9i7), with square bars instead of L-shaped ones, throughout the entire country. They will however almost never have more than two connecting wires.

images.caption: Poles by a road; the red circle zooms in on a ladder-like top of two bars with thin wires

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Two tall metal bars with L-shaped section joined by several thin wires like a ladder. Unique to the capital area. Similar tops with square bars exist elsewhere, but with at most two wires.

clues.title: Pole: square metal mesh
text: **Square metal mesh poles** are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.
NOTE: Most of the poles found outside of the Zamboanga peninsula are found along highways and have poletops with [three hanging insulators](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Tjfv9YpHyA3eSqoNA).

images.caption: Metal mesh pole in the distance; the red circle zooms in on it, left

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Square metal mesh poles on the big southern island, mainly its western peninsula. Elsewhere on the island, highway poles have three hanging insulators.

clues.title: Region: majority Muslim area in the south-west
text: While most of the Philippines is strongly Christian, a region of western Mindanao is majority **Muslim**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most of the country is strongly Christian, but a region of the south-west is mostly Muslim.

clues.title: Decoration: neon-green soda-bottle decorations
text: Decorations made of neon-green **Mountain Dew bottles** are commonly found in the north, particularly on northern Luzon.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Decorations made of neon-green soda bottles are common in the north, especially the main northern island.

clues.title: Vehicle: improvised farm tractor
text: This type of tractor, called a [kuliglig](https://noypicollections.blogspot.com/2011/07/improvised-vehicle-in-northern-luzon.html), is mostly found on the plains around Cauayan on northern Luzon.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A homemade-looking tractor called a kuliglig, mostly on the plains of the north.

clues.title: Landscape: round grassy hills over brown soil
text: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have [dark brown soil](https://www.google.com/maps/@9.8929167,124.09105,3a,15y,134.64h,94.67t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sAx3Neg240pCWv6JHjQpPDQ!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu) beneath the grass, earning them the name of [Chocolate Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocolate_Hills).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the centre: distinct round grassy hills with dark brown soil underneath.

clues.title: Landscape: lone volcano among flat fields
text: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A volcano completely surrounded by flat farmland.

clues.title: Landscape: smooth cone volcano, often in cloud
text: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect **smooth cone shape**. Beware that it will very often be covered in [clouds](https://goo.gl/maps/vVLbxF6FtgkXgyRk6).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: One of the tallest mountains, with an almost perfect smooth cone shape, but often hidden in clouds.

clues.title: Houses: destroyed buildings and ruins
text: In and around the city of Marawi, Mindanao you can find many destroyed houses and ruins from the [Marawi siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Marawi) in 2017.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Many destroyed houses and ruins from a siege in 2017, in and around one southern city.

clues.title: Landmark: large decorated white waystones
text: These large decorated white waystones, commemorating the [Bataan Death March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bataan_Death_March), can be seen along roads going from [Mariveles](https://maps.app.goo.gl/BJcyas8RAYUKhYgv9) and [Bagac](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3BfLZHBPRJogywTB8) in the south to [San Fernando](https://maps.app.goo.gl/RQpRQ69K63Lxzvbf8) in the north.
NOTE: The Bataan Death March continued from San Fernando to Capas by train, where a [larger memorial](https://maps.app.goo.gl/78N5YwJE9SDQm4Gr6) has been built.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Large decorated white waystones for a World War II death march, along roads from the south to the north of one peninsula. A bigger memorial is further north.

clues.title: Road: very wide, six lanes, little traffic
text: The highway going south from Puerto Princesa on Palawan can be characterised by being very wide, often featuring six lanes, while simultaneously having very little traffic.
Along the road you will usually see this [double electrical wire](https://maps.app.goo.gl/7VB1HRxdQfBNCKWG6), which can help confirm your guess.

images.caption: Very wide concrete road with little traffic; circle at upper left marks overhead wires

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A very wide highway, often six lanes, with very little traffic, and a double electrical wire along it. It leads south from a western island city.

clues.title: Pole: yellow lamp posts with black stripes
text: Lamp posts on Siquijor are typically painted **yellow**, with **black stripes** at the bottom.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Lamp posts painted yellow with black stripes at the bottom, on one small central island.

clues.title: Landmark: Roman soldier statues
text: Images and statues of ancient **Roman soldiers** can be found on the island of Marinduque.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Images and statues of ancient Roman soldiers, on one small island south of the main northern island.

clues.title: Google car: black with roof rack
text: You may find this **black** Street View car with a visible **roof rack** in and around the city of General Santos.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A black car with a visible roof rack, in and around one southern city.

clues.title: Google car: tape on the back
text: In northwestern Bohol you can find this Street View car with **tape** on the back.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A car with tape on the back, in the north-west of one central island.

clues.title: Google car: orange with visible side mirrors
text: An **orange** Street View car with visible side mirrors can be found on Corregidor Island.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: An orange car with visible side mirrors, on a small island at the mouth of a bay.

clues.title: Vehicle: thick black bars
text: This vehicle with several thick **black bars** can be found just south of the Mayon Volcano.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A vehicle with several thick black bars, seen just south of a famous volcano.

clues.title: Road: concrete and right-hand traffic
text: If you're in Southeast Asia and see concrete roads, you're most likely in the Philippines, Thailand, or, much more rarely, Indonesia. If you're driving on the right side, it will be the Philippines, while driving on the left side indicates Thailand or Indonesia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: In Southeast Asia, concrete roads mean mostly here or Thailand, rarely Indonesia. Right-hand traffic means it is here; left-hand means Thailand or Indonesia.

differs.how: Thailand also has concrete roads but drives on the left
Indonesia also drives on the left

clues.title: Google car: silver truck with roof rack (old coverage)
text: In southern Mindanao, in the very South of the Philippines, there is some footage taken with a silver truck with a visible roof rack. Note that this is leftover, unculled old coverage that runs parallel to gen 4 images of the same locations, so you can still get the same roads with a different car.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: In the far south, some old leftover coverage was shot with a silver truck with a roof rack. It runs alongside newer Gen 4 photos of the same roads.

clues.title: Pole: four stacked disc insulators
text: If you see a quadruple pancake insulator on a pole top, you're going to be on the one road with coverage in Davao Occidental, along the coast, between approximately Don Marcelino and Bukid.

images.caption: Poles topped with four stacked disc insulators

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Four stacked pancake-shaped insulators on a pole top mean the single covered coastal road in the far south-east.

clues.title: Pole: two stacked disc insulators
text: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Double pancake insulators are very rare but most likely along the east coast of one eastern island.

clues.title: Pole: thick insulator stem
text: The stems on which insulators sit at the top of poles is commonly thick or encased in a plastic tube that makes it appear much thicker than usual on the island of Bohol.

images.caption: Poles with a thick insulator stem

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The stems under the insulators on pole tops are thick or wrapped in plastic tube, making them look thicker than normal. It is common on one central island.

clues.title: Pole: three ridges and a long extender
text: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in northwestern Leyte and northwestern Biliran.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: An insulator with three ridges plus a long extender at the top to hold the wire. Most common in the north-west of two eastern central islands.

clues.title: Pole: grey solid insulator with many small ridges
text: This grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks kind of solid is most common in and around Manila, but can rarely be found elsewhere.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks almost solid. Most common around the capital, rare elsewhere.

clues.title: Pole: insulator shaped like desert-planet buildings
text: This type of insulator that looks like the buildings on Tatooine is most common in northern Luzon and in and around Manila.

images.caption: Pole insulators shaped like desert-planet buildings, two close-ups

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: An insulator that looks like the buildings on a sci-fi desert planet. Most common in the north and around the capital.

clues.title: Pole: cylinder insulator with four ridges
text: This cylinder with four distinct ridges is most common in Ilocos Norte, but can also be found in southern Biliran.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A cylinder with four clear ridges. Most common in the far north-west, but also found in the south of one eastern island.

clues.title: Road: grey guard blocks with yellow edges
text: In northern Cebu, you will find gray concrete guard blocks with their edges or sides painted yellow. These are not the only guard blocks in the area, so don't discount northern Cebu if you see, for example, fully yellow concrete blocks or walls and blocks with diagonal black and yellow stripes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Grey concrete guard blocks with yellow edges or sides, in the north of one central island. Other block styles exist there too, like fully yellow ones or diagonal black-yellow stripes.

clues.title: Pole: electric meters on yellow boards
text: On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Electricity meters on yellow backboards, horizontal or vertical, metal or wood. Found on two neighbouring islands in the centre-west.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycle with single wide front window
text: The trikes on the island of Palawan are recognizable by their single wide front window. Many of them look as if they were cosplaying as cars, with emblems and everything.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Tricycles with one wide front window, many looking like small cars with emblems. Found on one long western island.

clues.title: Road: sloped concrete blocks with round stone spots
text: The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.

images.caption: Pink line marks the sloped concrete blocks with round stone spots

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Sloped concrete blocks covered in round spots made of small stones. Straight-edged or non-spotted blocks exist elsewhere, but this combination is only in the southern peninsula of one eastern province.

clues.title: Road: alternating red and blue guard blocks
text: In a small area on the isthmus of Quezon province, you will find alternating red and blue guard blocks.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Alternating red and blue guard blocks in a small area on the narrow neck of one eastern province.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycle with umbrella
text: These trikes with an umbrella are super common in Maguindanao, Misamis Occidental, and Lanao del Sur. Note that these are really the only trikes found in Cotabato city, so if there’s only these guys it’s a good clue for there.
NOTE: These are also very common in Cebu!

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Tricycles with an umbrella are very common in the south-west, and in one city they are the only kind. They are also very common on one central island.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycle with two-part crown roof
text: Tuk-Tuks with a crown roof can be found mostly in Northern Luzon. The crown consists of two separate parts, a "rectangular" part and a "crown-shaped" part. Some Tuk-Tuks elsewhere will have a wavy top, but are not made of two parts and thus are not crowns.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Tricycles with a crown roof made of a rectangular part and a crown-shaped part, mostly in the north. Wavy tops elsewhere are not made of two parts.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycle with flat roof
text: Flat roofs are mostly found in the south. If it's a three-wheeler (as seen on the leftmost), you're probably on Mindanao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Flat roofs are mostly in the south. A three-wheeler is probably on the big southern island.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycle with low roof
text: Low roof Tuk-Tuks are generally found in the North.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Low-roof tricycles are generally found in the north.

clues.title: Vehicle: tricycle with airplane-window, tilted roof
text: This trike shape is essentially the only variant seen on the entire Zamboanga Peninsula. What sticks out to me is the passenger window shape- it’s kind of like an airplane window. Other notable parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window.
It’s identifiable from the back as well from the singular window in the back, as well as the roof tilting, and the random bars on top.

A common variant is this one with a large window hanging over the driver’s side. You can tell it’s the same type of trike from the same shape of the passenger car- where it has the airplane window (even if it’s horizontal) and then the bit beneath it that’s completely vertical and flat, along with the roof tilting back.
